name: Pause Deadlift
description: The pause deadlift involves a deliberate hold at the sticking point — typically mid-shin height — during the ascent phase of the conventional deadlift. The pause eliminates momentum and forces the musculature to generate maximum force from a static position, building strength at the most mechanically challenging portion of the lift. It is a highly effective strength-building variation for powerlifters targeting their weakest point in the pull.

execution.starting_position: Set up identically to a conventional deadlift. Bar over mid-foot, neutral spine, hips below shoulders.
execution.setup_instructions: Use 70-85% of conventional deadlift maximum. Mark the mid-shin position visually before starting.
steps: Step 1: Initiate the deadlift identically to conventional — drive the legs and maintain back angle.
Step 2: When the bar reaches mid-shin height, pause completely for 2-3 seconds.
Step 3: Maintain maximum tightness during the pause — no relaxing.
Step 4: Drive through the pause and complete the lift to lockout.
Step 5: Return the bar to the floor under control and reset before the next rep.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before each rep. Hold the brace through the pause. Exhale at lockout.
common_mistakes: Losing tension during the pause — the hold must be active, not passive
Using too heavy a load, which forces the bar to move through the pause
Pausing at the wrong point — it should be mid-shin, the actual sticking point
safety_considerations: Reduce training load significantly from conventional deadlift maximum
Ensure consistent breath holding and bracing before each rep
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Floor to lockout. Pause position is at mid-shin, which is the sticking point for most lifters.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 1-0-pause(2-3s)-0 (explosive off floor, hold at mid-shin, then drive through)
coaching_cues: Don't relax at the pause — stay tight
The pause is where you get stronger
Drive through the pause like it's a new rep
